title: “Standing on the Corner” by The Four Lads
text: "Standing on the Corner" is a popular song written by Frank Loesser and published in 1956. It was introduced by Shorty Long, Alan Gilbert, John Henson, and Roy Lazarus in the Broadway musical, The Most Happy Fella.

title: “The Flying Saucer” by Buchanan & Goodman
text: "The Flying Saucer" is a novelty record, the first of a series of break-in records released by Bill Buchanan and Dickie Goodman (credited simply as "Buchanan & Goodman"). The song is considered to be an early (perhaps the earliest) example of a mashup, featuring segments of popular songs intertwined with spoken "news" commentary to tell the story of a visit from a flying saucer.

title: “Ivory Tower” by Cathy Carr
text: "Ivory Tower" is a popular song written by Jack Fulton and Lois Steele. Popular versions by Cathy Carr and Gale Storm, and a rhythm & blues version by Otis Williams all received major popularity in 1956.

title: “See You Later Alligator” by Bill Haley & His Comets
text: "See You Later, Alligator" is a 1950s rock and roll song written and first recorded by American singer-songwriter Bobby Charles. The song was a top ten hit for Bill Haley and His Comets in 1956 in the United States, reaching no.

title: “I'll Be Home” by Pat Boone
text: "I'll Be Home" is a 1955 song that was written by Ferdinand Washington and songwriter, Stan Lewis. Both the Flamingos and the Pat Boone versions feature a spoken recitation of the Bridge section.

title: “On the Street Where You Live” by Vic Damone
text: "On the Street Where You Live" is a song with music by Frederick Loewe and lyrics by Alan Jay Lerner from the 1956 Broadway musical My Fair Lady. It is sung in the musical by the character Freddy Eynsford-Hill, who was portrayed by John Michael King in the original production.

title: “(You've Got) The Magic Touch” by The Platters
text: " The Magic Touch" is a song written by Buck Ram, and performed by The Platters. It reached #4 on both the U.S. pop chart and the U.S. R&B chart in 1956.

title: “Born to Be with You” by The Chordettes
text: "Born to Be with You" is a song by the American female vocal quartet The Chordettes. Written by Don Robertson, the song was released in 1956.
listen: Born to Be with You The Chordettes

title: “Band of Gold” by Don Cherry
text: "Band of Gold" is a traditional pop song, with music by Jack Taylor and lyrics by Bob Musel. It was published in 1955.

title: “More” by Perry Como
text: "More" is a popular song with music by Alex Alstone and lyrics by Tom Glazer, published in 1956. The best-known version of the song was recorded by Perry Como on May 8, 1956, alongside, Mitchell Ayres and His Orchestra and The Ray Charles Singers.
wiki: More (Alex Alstone and Tom Glazer song)

title: “Singing the Blues” by Guy Mitchell
text: "Singing the Blues" is a popular song composed by Melvin Endsley and published in 1956. The highest-charting version was by Guy Mitchell and the first recording of the song was by Marty Robbins.

title: “Blueberry Hill” by Fats Domino
text: "Blueberry Hill" is a popular American song published in 1940 and first recorded and released by Sammy Kaye in 1940 on RCA Victor. It is best remembered for its 1950s rock and roll version by Fats Domino.

title: “The Happy Whistler” by Don Robertson
text: "The Happy Whistler" is a song written and performed by Don Robertson. It reached #6 on the U.S. pop chart and #8 on the UK Singles Chart in 1956.

title: “True Love” by Bing Crosby & Grace Kelly
text: "True Love" is a popular song written by American songwriter Cole Porter, published in 1956. The song was introduced by Bing Crosby and Grace Kelly in the musical film High Society.
listen: True Love Bing Crosby & Grace Kelly

title: “Long Tall Sally” by Little Richard
text: "Long Tall Sally", also known as "Long Tall Sally", is a rock and roll song written by Robert "Bumps" Blackwell, Enotris Johnson, and Little Richard and released on Richard's album Here's Little Richard. Richard recorded it for Specialty Records, which released it as a single in March 1956, backed with "Slippin' and Slidin'".

title: “A Sweet Old Fashioned Girl” by Teresa Brewer
text: "A Sweet Old Fashioned Girl" is a song written by Bob Merrill. The song was produced by Dick Jacobs, and performed by Teresa Brewer.

title: “Transfusion” by Nervous Norvus
text: Jimmy Drake, known professionally as Nervous Norvus, was an American musician known for the controversial novelty song "Transfusion".

title: “It Only Hurts for a Little While” by The Ames Brothers
text: "It Only Hurts for a Little While" is a 1956 popular song with music by Fred Spielman and lyrics by Mack David. The recording by The Ames Brothers was released by RCA Victor Records as catalog number 20-6481.

title: “A Tear Fell” by Teresa Brewer
text: "A Tear Fell" is a popular song. It was written by Eugene Randolph and Dorian Burton and released in 1956.

title: “Rock Island Line” by Lonnie Donegan
text: "Rock Island Line" is an American folk song about the railroad of the same name. The song was originally sung as a spiritual by slaves on the plantations of the Mississippi River Valley, and was first transcribed as a folk song in 1929.
